title: steering-state-reconciliation-controller-notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a working design for a reconciliation-first steering controller that unifies intent-driven multi-region traffic steering for our control plane. Aim: reduce incorrect rapid failovers, make rollouts deterministic, and allow hybrid use of GeoDNS and Anycast while keeping regional preference and capacity-aware fallback simple to reason about.

Context / motivation:
- We have competing mechanisms for steering: Anycast for low-latency routing, GeoDNS for coarse region affinity, and control-plane level routing policies (weights, preferences).
- Operational pain: rapid flips during partial outages, conflicting overrides from ops vs automated policies, and difficulty reasoning about eventual state when components disagree.
- Goal: single source of truth for steering intent (what we want), and a reconciler that translates that into region-specific runtime actions (DNS records, BGP hints, egress policies) with explicit rollout windows and safety checks.

Non-goals:
- This is not a replacement for BGP/peering ops or wholesale Anycast redesign.
- Not handling per-customer private networking (that stays in private-deployments team).

Requirements (high-level):
1) Intent model: expressive enough to encode region preference, fallback priority list, weight targets, and per-region capacity constraints.
2) Reconcilability: controller must converge from any divergent state to the intent-safe state with idempotent steps.
3) Safety: detect and pause rollouts when telemetry shows overload or degraded request success rates.
4) Traceability: every steering action must be auditable (who + why + revision).
5) Hybrid app: support both GeoDNS and Anycast as actuators; controller decides which actuator to touch and how.

Key concepts / vocabulary:
- Intent: declarative object (region-preference, weights, failover-order, capacity-thresholds).
- Actuator: concrete system we modify (DNS provider, Anycast BGP controller, edge-config push).
- Projection: actuator-specific representation of the intent (e.g., DNS weights or BGP locality hints).
- Revision: monotonically increasing integer on intent; used to ensure ordering.
- Guard: health check rule that can block or roll back a projection.

Data model (proposal):
Intent fields (flat):
- id: string (human readable)
- revision: string (wallclock or semver-like e.g. r20251118-3)
- primary_regions: comma-separated list of region codes (e.g., us-west1, eu-central1)
- fallback_order: comma-separated list (ordered)
- weight_targets: semi-colon list of region:percent e.g. us-west1:60;eu-central1:40
- min_capacity_pct: string (e.g., "30")
- ttl_seconds: string (DNS TTL suggestion)
- actuator_preferences: comma-separated (anycast,dns)
- metadata: free-text short note

(We intentionally keep everything string/list-of-strings to keep storage simple and to match existing config surfaces.)

Reconciler architecture (components):
1) Intent Store (control plane): small consistent store (etcd-like) that authoring tools write intents into. Each intent has a revision and metadata.
2) Decision Engine: evaluates current telemetry (healthy endpoints, capacity utilisation, error budgets) + intent => desired projections per actuator. Runs evaluation policy in read-only mode first (preview).
3) Execution Engine (Actuator Workers): for each actuator (DNS provider, BGP controller, edge-config), a worker applies the projection using idempotent APIs and writes back status.
4) Reconciler Loop: periodically (every 5s by default) compare projection status to desired; take small, reversible steps toward the projection.
5) Guardrails/Tokens: token bucket per-region to throttle how fast weight changes can happen to avoid thrashing.

Reconciliation semantics (important):
- Convergence is stepwise: prefer small delta updates. For weights, change at most 10% or 50 tokens per minute (configurable).
- All actuator changes are stamped with the intent revision and an operation id. If a newer revision is observed, ongoing operations are aborted and a new plan is computed.
- Health guards: if any region crosses error rate threshold (>3% 5m) or latency P90 doubles from baseline, pause further changes and optionally roll back the last step.

Example projection mapping rules (informal):
- If actuator_preferences contains "anycast" and anycast region is healthy => push locality hints (BGP MED/communities) to prefer primaries.
- If DNS actuator is used: compute per-region DNS weights from weight_targets but apply step-wise damping. TTL set to max(300, intent.ttl_seconds).
- If capacity in a region < min_capacity_pct => mark region as disabled and remove from active pool in both Anycast and DNS projections.

Decision heuristics (sketch):
- Input signals: region capacity % (normalized), recent error rate, average latency, instance count, backlog metric.
- Compute score S_region = alpha * capacity_norm + beta * (1 - error_rate_norm) + gamma * (1 - latency_norm). Tune alpha/beta/gamma in rollout.
- If S_primary_region < threshold => trigger failover to next fallback region with a weighted ramp.

Runbook snippets (ops-facing):
- Quick rollback: set intent.revision to previous revision and mark "force: true" in metadata; controller will fast-path revert to previous projection but will still respect guard limits unless "force-override" is set.
- Emergency blackhole: if a region is observed to blackhole (SYNs accepted but no responses), immediate action: remove from anycast peering table and set DNS weight to 0 (if DNS update TTL <= 60). Notify SRE.

Pseudocode: reconcile loop (simplified)

for intent in intent_store.list():
  if intent.revision <= last_seen_revision(intent.id):
    continue
  desired = decision_engine.compute(intent, telemetry_snapshot)
  for actuator in desired.actuators:
    current = actuator_worker.get_status(intent.id, actuator)
    plan = diff_and_plan(current, desired[actuator], step_limit)
    if plan.requires_pause_due_to_health():
      emit_event("pause", intent.id)
      continue
    actuator_worker.apply(plan, intent.revision)
  mark_revision_applied(intent.id, intent.revision)

Operational scenarios (short):
1) Region overloaded during promotional surge: controller sees capacity dip below min_capacity_pct -> reduces weight incrementally, ramps up fallback regions, guards prevent >20% weight shift per 10m.
2) Regional API control-plane partition: anycast may continue delivering to same POPs but Edge config mismatches cause errors -> controller will detect error spikes and pause; ops notified to investigate; DNS weights left unchanged until explicit operator action.

Conflict resolution model:
- Intents are authoritative. Manual operator overrides create a new intent with higher revision (auditable).
- If two intents with same id but different authors arrive concurrently, tie-breaker is revision timestamp; controller will notify owners and refuse auto-merge.

Telemetry and observability needs:
- Per-region: request count, 5m error rate, p50/p90 latency, queue/backlog, instance count, GPU utilisation where applicable.
- Events stream: intent-applied, intent-paused, actuator-error, rollback, emergency-block.
- Dashboards: intent state timeline, weight transitions, actuator sync latencies.

Safety checklist before broad rollout:
- Integration tests for idempotent actuator calls (mock DNS, mock BGP controller).
- Chaos tests: simulate region blackhole and network partitions.
- Canaries: roll out to a single low-traffic intent first; verify telemetry and rollback behavior.

Open questions / TODOs:
- What should the default step_limit be for weight changes? (10% vs absolute token counts)
- Should we maintain per-customer intents (multi-tenancy) or collapse to a tenancy-aggregated intent for global steering? (tradeoff: granularity vs complexity)
- Anycast actuator: to what extent can we programmatically alter BGP attributes in each cloud provider? Ops needs to own the final switch for provider-level peering changes.
- Does the DNS provider support sub-minute TTLs reliably in all regions? If not, controller needs to prefer Anycast for fast failover.

Action items / next milestones:
- [ ] Implement intent schema storage and revisioning (owner: Darren)
- [ ] Prototype decision engine with synthetic telemetry (owner: Evan)
- [ ] Build actuator mock suite (owner: Marta)
- [ ] Run tabletop for SRE + NetEng to validate emergency procedures (owner: Asha)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the intent model intentionally simple and stringy so product teams can author via CLI quickly.
- Avoid building overly-smart rollback heuristics early; prefer manual checkpoints until telemetry proves reliable.
- This controller should be pluggable — other teams might want to add a custom actuator (e.g., partner-cdn).

References / links: see linked_artifacts above. Also: internal slack thread #platform-regional-steering (search for thread id: 2025-11-steer-3)

Draft status: rough draft for architecture review. Expect multiple iterations after we get feedback from NetEng about Anycast actuation boundaries and from SRE on the health thresholds.

-- Asha
